title: A Bad Day for a Small Person

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — GOOD, BAD AND ORDINARY DAYS (DAY-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Wonderful days, rotten days, mixed days and days when nothing much happens at all. Moods come without reasons, small things matter more than they should, and nobody has to end the day happier, wiser or more productive than they started it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a child aged 4-9 and an adult)
the owner (2026-11-15): a person named by a role word is a cast villager and shows the name (flavor only: the villager need not have that job)

collection.description: A small child has had a very bad day and sits glaring at the ground: listen to all of it, or offer a small treat.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has had a bad day. (subject.He/she) lost a race, dropped (subject.his/her) fruit in the sand, got told off for splashing, and (child), a bigger child, said (subject.his/her) sandcastle was "just a lump." (subject.He/she) is sitting outside the hut with (subject.his/her) knees pulled up, glaring at the ground. (friend) sits down beside (subject.him/her).

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: "Tell me," says (friend). (subject) tells (friend.him/her). All of it. In great detail. With several additions. (friend) listens to every word and says, at the end, "That does sound like a very bad day." (subject) nods hard. Then, because someone has finally understood, (subject.he/she) leans against (friend) and is quiet.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: (friend) doesn't ask anything. (friend.He/she) goes inside and comes out with a little honey on a leaf. (subject) eats it, still glaring. The glare gets smaller. It doesn't go away completely. "It was still a bad day," says (subject). "I know," says (friend). "Tomorrow's a different one."
